reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people is one of Yahweh's goals. Most directly, Yahweh commands David: 'You shall feed my people Israel, and you shall be leader over Israel' (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה לְךָ אַתָּה תִרְעֶה אֶת־ עַמִּי אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאַתָּה תִּהְיֶה לְנָגִיד עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), explicitly commissioning David as shepherd of His people. Additionally, Yahweh actively assists Israel by delivering the Philistines into David's hand in battle ('I will certainly give the Philistines into your hand'), and the narrative shows Yahweh blessing the people and restoring proper worship of the Ark. These actions collectively demonstrate Yahweh's goal to provide leadership, military deliverance, and spiritual blessing to the Hebrew people.
